_comment: How the game turns the map data in data/city/ into a town. Coordinates are never typed here: places are named by the streets that meet there, and the game looks them up in the OSM data.

origin._comment: World (0,0,0). This is the OSM position of the Great George Street / Richmond Street junction (node 8598664). Keep it fixed when the map grows so existing coordinates stay valid.

play_area._comment: The playable area: the bypass ring (Riverside Drive, the Arterial Highway, Upton Road), closed by the North River and the harbour. 'ring' goes round the edge in order: 'streets' is a junction named by two streets that meet there, and between two such junctions the edge follows the shortest way along the streets in 'follow' ("" lets it through the unnamed roundabouts on Riverside Drive). 'water' is a point out in the river or harbour as [latitude, longitude], the one place coordinates are typed, since water has no street names. The invisible wall sits margin_m outside this line, with road-closed barriers wherever a street crosses it.

ring._comment: the North River, where the Trans-Canada crosses to Cornwall
the Hillsborough River, past the bridge

spawn._comment: The player starts on the sidewalk at this junction, facing the 'face_toward' junction.

parked_cars._comment: Cars parked at the start, against the right-hand curb: on 'street', 'distance_m' from the junction with 'from', heading toward 'toward'. 'model' is an id in scripts/vehicles/car_models.gd; 'colour' is a hex colour or the model's first colour if left out.

road_defaults._comment: By OSM highway class: curb-to-curb width (two-way and one-way), sidewalk width, and for highways the paved shoulder outside the edge line. When OSM gives a lane count the width is lanes x lane + both shoulders. A class with a shoulder is built highway style: no curbs or sidewalks, white edge lines, gravel verges.

street_overrides._comment: Widths measured against OSM building footprints (median gap between building fronts across each street, inside the play area). Curb + sidewalk must stay inside that gap.

brick_streets._comment: Victoria Row: the brick block of Richmond Street between Queen and Great George.

landmarks._comment: Extra detail for well-known buildings, matched by OSM way id. Footprints still come from OSM; these set what the footprint can't tell us. Colours, heights and towers are best estimates, not measurements. Entries can be small: one that only sets colours or materials keeps the building's measured lidar height and roof (set wall_height or roof to override those). Keys: style (brick, clapboard, sandstone, painted, modern, shingle, church), colour, roof_colour, spire_colour, wall_height (m), roof (flat or gabled), pitch (degrees), trim (white, cream, green, black), shop, awning (a colour, or none), towers (front_pair, front_center, front_corner), tower_size, tower_height, spire_height, tower_protrude (m), portico, portico_width, and where the front is: front_toward [street, street] (faces that junction) or front_street.

_heritage_comment: heritage_district_m: buildings and streets within this many metres of the origin get the downtown look (Victorian brick blocks and shopfronts, black cast-iron lamp posts). Elsewhere: houses, plain modern boxes for big buildings, and street lights on wooden poles.
